Everywhere I look it is all tablets, pens and touch screens. Are we creating an epidemic chronic pain in people that use these devices?

The ergonomics of a keyboard are not perfect either. The best developments of keyboard technology (Ergodox et. al.) are coming just as the technology is starting to fade.

There were three key technologies developed at the end of the steam era that made the steam engines much more efficient. These were the poppet valve, the closed crankcase and the pressure lubrication. All three were first applied to the steam engines. This resulted in marvels of efficiency like the Willans high speed engine. Alas, the technology came too late and was only understood and applied to the internal combustion engines. The steam engines on the liberty ships of WWII had none of these developments.

The same thing is happening to keyboards. The improvements are coming, but it is too late. I too did work on my own switch design for a while but abandoned the idea because I think it is fruitless.

There is also the problem of semantics which is much deeper than the keyboard itself. Why do I need to press 6 keys in order to type a simple "Hello" ? That is 40 bits in UTF-8. More than 1 trillion possibilities.

Surely we can encode all the words and all the concepts in every language with 40 bits! So why do we need to encode them letter by letter? Wouldn't it be better if we could encode the concepts directly? That would let us translate every language to another language directly on semantic level. Think of the possibilities! But if we try that the keyboard would fail us miserably. So keyboards are holding us back in this case.

Lastly there is the problem of scope. Keyboards can only handle type. There are lots of things that we deal with on our computers which are not type, pictures, maps, video, sound, 3D geometry, fields, vectors and so on. Some of these things can only barely be described by type using some sort of a markup language and some are entirely impossible. We need user interfaces which are better at handling these things.

Sorry for the long rant.
